extracted.intended_audience: state policymakers, state higher-education authorizing agencies, and higher-education policy analysts
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluation criteria for how state authorizing agencies should monitor, require, and disclose postsecondary institutional performance and outcomes; includes recommendations on reporting frequency, data standards, disclosure, and enforcement. Geared to improving consumer protection and regulatory effectiveness across U.S. states.

rubrics_metrics.name: Require outcomes data at initial authorization
rubrics_metrics.description: Most state authorizers do not require outcomes data from colleges when they initially apply for authorization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The report identifies the absence of required outcomes at application as a gap. Recommendation implication: states should require institutions to provide outcomes metrics as part of initial authorization applications so that approvals consider performance, not only inputs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Require regular (annual or reauthorization) outcomes reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: A majority of agencies compile student outcomes either during reauthorization or through annual reports, but roughly a third of authorizers do not require any outcomes information on an annual basis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: States should mandate periodic reporting of outcomes (annual or at reauthorization intervals) so regulators maintain up-to-date information on performance. The report flags current uneven practice across agencies as problematic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publicly disclose outcomes data for authorized institutions
rubrics_metrics.description: Most authorizing agencies do not disclose outcomes data annually for all authorized institutions; only a handful publicize reported student outcomes for all institutions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authorizers should disclose outcomes to students, parents, and the public to support consumer protection and informed enrollment decisions. The report notes that while many agencies require institutions to disclose outcomes to prospective enrollees, agency-level public disclosure is less common.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implement explicit minimum performance thresholds
rubrics_metrics.description: Few state authorizers have explicit minimum performance standards for institutions (such as a minimum completion rate or retention rate).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The report recommends developing minimum performance thresholds to help identify and sanction poorly performing schools. Such thresholds would make performance expectations transparent and enable enforcement actions where institutions fall below standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Require and disclose program-level outcomes (in addition to institution-level)
rubrics_metrics.description: Authorizers should require and disclose program-level outcomes measurements, not just institution-level aggregates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Program-level data give finer-grained information useful to consumers and regulators; the report explicitly recommends requiring and publishing program-level outcomes alongside institutional metrics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standardize outcomes definitions and measurements across agencies
rubrics_metrics.description: Definitions of outcome measurements vary from agency to agency, producing inconsistent data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Work to standardize outcomes reporting across agencies—potentially using existing state authorization reciprocity agreements as a vehicle for producing common definitions for student outcomes measurements—so data are comparable and meaningful across states.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimize institutional reporting burden and link to administrative data
rubrics_metrics.description: Authorizers should rely less on institutions to report certain outcomes indicators and instead require only basic, essential reported data from institutions, then link that information to independently verifiable administrative data sources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reduce duplicative reporting by obtaining outcomes from state administrative databases (e.g., unemployment insurance, wage records, state K–12/higher-ed data systems) to improve accuracy and lower institutional burden.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verify reliability of institution-reported data
rubrics_metrics.description: There are concerns about the reliability of the data reported to state agencies by institutions, particularly when self-reported.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: States should implement verification and validation procedures (or prefer administrative data sources) to ensure accuracy of reported outcomes before using them for public disclosure or regulatory decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use outcomes as a factor in authorization and reauthorization decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: It is not clear that indicators of performance are a factor in agencies’ authorization decisions; authorizers rarely renew authorizations based on indicators of performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: States should explicitly include outcomes indicators in authorization and reauthorization standards and decisionmaking, rather than focusing primarily on inputs (faculty, facilities, curricula). Doing so aligns oversight with actual institutional performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Require institutions to disclose student outcomes to prospective enrollees
rubrics_metrics.description: Numerous agencies require institutions themselves to disclose student outcomes to prospective enrollees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure that disclosure requirements for institutions are clear, standardized, and enforced so prospective students receive consistent, usable information about completion, placement, and other outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider multi-state performance when authorizing multi-state institutions
rubrics_metrics.description: Question whether states consider institutions’ outcomes in other states when those institutions are seeking authorization in their state.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For institutions operating across state lines (e.g., online providers), authorizers should review outcomes from other states in which the institution operates to get a fuller picture of performance and consumer risk.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide clear sanctions and enforcement for poor-performing institutions
rubrics_metrics.description: Are there repercussions for poor-performing institutions? Few authorizers have explicit minimum performance standards or clear sanctioning mechanisms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: States should define and publicize consequences for failing performance (e.g., probation, loss of authorization, fines), and link monitoring and disclosure frameworks to enforcement tools so poor performance leads to corrective action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Shift emphasis from inputs toward outcomes in oversight
rubrics_metrics.description: State authorization processes overwhelmingly consider inputs—faculty qualifications, facilities, equipment—when approving new colleges; states rarely renew authorizations based on performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The ideal regulatory system should monitor and disclose institutional performance (outcomes) to protect consumers; authorizers should rebalance oversight to emphasize outcomes over inputs where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use reciprocity agreements to reduce burden and harmonize standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Efforts such as the State Authorization Reciprocity Agreement exist to lighten compliance and regulatory loads for schools and state agencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: States should consider leveraging interstate reciprocity agreements to harmonize outcome definitions and reporting requirements and reduce duplicate authorization burdens for multi-state institutions, while preserving states' rights to enforce consumer protection laws.
